title: Email verification
subtitle: Members confirm an email address with a code, and get roles that depend on it or on the invite they used.
unavailable: The server has no LLM_KEY_SECRET, so email verification cannot be used yet.

overview.smtpNotReady: Not set up. Ask the bot owner to set the mail server.

settings.title: Settings
settings.defaultRolesHelp: Every verified member gets these, on top of the roles of the rules that match. At most {max}.
settings.unverifiedRoleHelp: Given to members who are not verified yet; taken away once they are verified.
settings.logChannelHelp: Gets a line for every verification, without the address.
settings.verifyMessageHelp: Shown to members who press the verify button. Leave empty for the built-in text. At most {max} characters.
settings.autoVerifyOnJoin: Send the button to new members
settings.autoVerifyOnJoinHelp: By direct message. Members who closed their messages will not get it.
settings.autoUnverifiedOnJoin: Give new members the unverified role

rules.title: Access rules
rules.intro: A rule gives roles when its condition holds. Conditions combine fields with AND and OR, in groups. With no rule that looks at an email address, any valid address is accepted.

help.title: How conditions work
help.fields: Fields: domain (the part after the @, such as *.edu), email (the whole address, such as *@hcmus.edu.vn), list (an email list by name) and invite (the invite link the member joined with). * stands for any text.
help.example2: Example: domain:*.edu OR list:k21 OR email:*@hcmus.edu.vn
help.precedence: AND binds tighter than OR; use parentheses to group. A rule that only looks at the invite gives its roles as soon as the member joins; the others apply after the email is verified.
help.invite: Telling which invite a member used needs the bot to have the Manage Server permission.

rules.textInvalid: The condition cannot be read: {reason} (at position {position}).

errors.EXPECTED_CONDITION: a condition such as domain:*.edu is missing
errors.UNKNOWN_FIELD: unknown field, use domain, email, list or invite
errors.INVALID_VALUE: the value is not valid for its field
errors.TOO_MANY_TERMS: too many conditions in one rule

rules.missingLists: These lists do not exist, so their conditions never hold: {names}
rules.removeConfirm: Remove this rule? Members already verified keep their roles.
rules.empty: No rules yet. Any valid address is accepted and gets only the default roles.
rules.full: This server has the most rules it can have ({max}).
rules.fixErrors: Fix the rules marked below before saving.
rules.unsavedChanges: You have changes that are not saved.

tester.title: Try an email address
tester.intro: Check what the rules above would do, before you save them. The result uses the same matching as the bot.
tester.empty: Type an address to see the result.

results.NOT_ACCEPTED: Not accepted: no rule that looks at the address holds

tester.listNote: A list condition cannot be checked here, because lists keep only hashes; it counts as not holding.
tester.skipped: {count} rule(s) with errors are left out of this check.

blocklist.title: Blocklist
blocklist.intro: Addresses that match one of these patterns are refused, whatever the rules say. * stands for any text, for example *@mailinator.com.
blocklist.help: Type a pattern and press Enter. Lower case, at most {max} patterns.
blocklist.invalid: These patterns are not valid: {patterns}. Use letters, digits and . _ % + * ' @ -.

lists.title: Email lists
lists.intro: A list holds addresses a rule can refer to with list:name. Addresses are kept only as hashes; they cannot be read back.
lists.name: Name
lists.deleteConfirm: Delete the list {name}? Rules that use it stop matching.
lists.full: This server has the most lists it can have ({max}).
lists.addEmailsHelp: Paste addresses separated by spaces, commas, semicolons, | or new lines, or upload a CSV or TXT file. Big lists are sent in several parts.
lists.clearConfirm: Remove every address from the list {name}?
lists.entriesFull: A list holds at most {max} addresses.
lists.fileTooLarge: The file is larger than {max} MB.
lists.fileUnreadable: The file could not be read.
lists.noEmails: There is no address to send yet.
lists.tooManyEntries: A list holds at most {max} addresses. This one has {count} and you are adding up to {adding}.

members.title: Verified members
members.intro: Addresses are kept encrypted and only managers of this server see them.
members.manualHelp: Confirms the address without sending a code and gives the matching roles.
members.revokeConfirm: Remove the verification of {name}? The roles it gave are taken away.
members.exportConfirm: The file lists every verified member with email address, Discord name and roles. It contains personal data: keep it safe and do not share it.
members.exportFailed: The export could not be created. Please try again.

button.title: Verify button
button.intro: Posts a message with a button in a channel. Members press it to start verifying.
button.defaultHelp: Leave a field empty to use the built-in text.
button.channelRequired: Pick the channel to post in.
button.confirmPlan: A message with the verify button will be posted in #{channel}, as in the preview.

smtp.title: Mail server
smtp.intro: The one SMTP account the bot sends verification emails through, for every server.
smtp.adminOnly: The mail server is set up from the bot owner's own server only.
smtp.secure: Use TLS from the start (usually port 465)
smtp.passwordHelp: Leave empty to keep the stored password.
smtp.testOk: The mail server accepted the connection.

testFailed.unreachable: The mail server could not be reached.
testFailed.auth: The mail server refused the username or password.
testFailed.rejected: The mail server refused the request.
testFailed.unresolved: The mail server name could not be found. Check the host name.

smtp.fromAddressHelp: The address the emails come from.
smtp.saveFirst: Save first, then test. The test uses the saved mail server.

errors.passwordAgain: Enter the password again for the new host.
